{"text":"Given this is a mobile quick-commerce app with purple branding (clearly established by the PDF), I'll go with a clean, functional approach. The Swiss stance suits this well - strict grid, one accent (purple), precise alignment. I'll use Inter for body text (clean, readable) and a slightly more characterful sans for headings. Let me commit to Swiss + modern mobile-first design with purple accent.

Now let me build the full app. This is a large undertaking - I'll create:

1. `src/index.css` - fonts and tokens
2. `src/App.tsx` - main router/state
3. Multiple screen components
4. A state management system to handle navigation between all the user and admin screens

I'm mapping out the full screen hierarchy: customer-facing flows like splash, authentication, product browsing, cart, and checkout, plus admin screens for managing orders, catalog, retailers, and delivery settings. I'll structure this as a single-page app with screen state management to keep transitions smooth.

For the design system, I'm using a purple color palette with #7C3AED as the primary, a subtle lavender background, and Inter font. The customer app will have a bottom navigation bar for the main sections, optimized for mobile at 430px max-width.

I'm deciding between putting everything in one large App.tsx file versus splitting screens into separate component files—I think separate files will be cleaner for maintainability, so I'll organize screens in a dedicated folder and use a simple state-based router in the main app.

Now I'm mapping out all the files I need to create: the core setup files like index.css and App.tsx, mock data, then each screen component for the customer flow (splash through order success), admin dashboard, and supporting screens like notifications and profile.

I'm realizing this is getting unwieldy with so many separate files, so I'm going to consolidate the admin screens into fewer files rather than creating individual components for each admin feature. Actually, I think I'll simplify this whole approach and build everything within a single App.tsx file to keep it manageable.

I'm going to start writing the code now, beginning with the app wrapper that displays a phone frame on desktop and goes full-screen on mobile.

Writing App.tsx... Writing Tailwind config... Creating all the screen components...

I'm noticing there's a lot of duplication in the admin screens, so I should consolidate some of these—like combining the add product and add category flows into modals within the catalog view, and merging retailer details into the main retailers screen rather than having separate detail pages.

The core screens I really need to focus on are Home, Cart, Checkout, and the Admin Dashboard. I should also make sure the app displays nicely on mobile (390px max width) with a phone frame effect on desktop, and I'll use a simple grid of colored divs to represent the QR code for UPI payments.

For navigation between screens, I'll implement smooth slide animations using CSS transforms to give it that native app feel. Now I'm ready to start writing out all the files—infrastructure first, then the screens.

I'm defining the screen type union that covers all 28 screens across both the customer and admin apps, and I need to think through how to pass navigation parameters like which category or product was selected, or which order is being viewed.

Now I'm planning the data structure—I'll need to define products with their categories, prices, and stock levels, plus orders, retailers in various approval states, and notifications. I'm going to write out the data file first, then build the context, then implement all the screens. I've also got my color palette locked in with purple as the primary color and a light purple-tinted background.

Looking at the navigation structure, the customer side needs a bottom tab bar for Home, Search, Orders, and Profile, while the admin panel will be simpler with just back navigation. I'm thinking about keeping the code organized by splitting screens into separate files but connecting them through context to keep the bundle manageable.

Writing the file structure now... Continuing through the rest of the inventory with coconut oil, then moving into pulses and lentils where toor dal is running low at just 8 units, followed by the spice section with turmeric, chili, and coriander powders all well-stocked. I'm also starting to see the orders section come through with the first entry for Sharma General Store.

Now I'm looking at the remaining orders in the pipeline—there's one out for delivery, one still pending, one that's already been delivered, and one that was cancelled. Then I'm reviewing the retailer accounts, with three approved partners showing their total sales and order counts, and seven more retailers waiting for approval.

I'm planning to build out the implementation now, starting with the styling and data structure, then moving through the context setup and main app component before tackling each screen. For the QR codes, I'll use a simple SVG pattern approach, and for the charts in the admin dashboard, I'll create basic CSS and SVG bar charts without needing an external charting library. I'm also thinking through how to handle screen transitions—I'll use a fade and slide animation with CSS to make the navigation feel smooth. I'll set up Tailwind v4 with a custom theme using `@theme` to define the purple primary color and its variants, then organize the project structure starting with the core files like types and styling before building out the components.

For screen transitions, I'm implementing CSS keyframe animations that slide screens in from the right or left depending on navigation direction, with opacity fading to create a smooth visual effect.

Writing animation styles... Writing the screen components... Defining the context methods and state... Adding cart management functions...

Now I'm wrapping everything in the context provider and exporting the hook to access it. Then I need to set up the data layer with categories, products with their pricing structures, orders, and retailers. Defining the type schemas... Account creation flow, pending approval screen with status check, then the retailer home with store header, delivery banner, stock alerts, and a scrollable buy-again section plus category grid. Moving into category and product detail screens with image backgrounds, pricing, stock info, and quantity controls, with a persistent cart bar throughout.

Search functionality with recent chips and results, then the cart page showing items with quantity adjusters and a minimum order warning, flowing into checkout with address form, location detection, and payment method selection between COD and UPI. The UPI payment screen displays the amount, QR code, and UPI ID for copying along with screenshot upload.

After payment, there's an order success screen with animation and order ID, followed by My Orders showing filterable tabs for different statuses and order cards with summaries. The order detail view includes a timeline stepper, full itemization, delivery address, and payment info with options to buy again or cancel.

Rounding out the app are notifications with read status indicators, and a profile section split between a store card with delivery address and business details like GST and hours, plus a settings tab for notification toggles, appearance modes, and account management.

For the admin side, there's a dashboard with pending approvals, retailer count, and today's orders displayed as stats cards, plus a bar chart showing the last week's order volume and a retailer approval queue. Admins can manage orders through filtered views and update status via dropdown, see all products and categories with low stock alerts and edit/delete controls, and toggle category visibility.

I'm also mapping out the forms for adding or editing products—image upload, name, category and unit selection, tiered pricing by quantity, stock level, and active status—and categories with similar image and name fields plus an active toggle. The retailer management section has separate tabs for approved and pending retailers, showing details like avatar, name, owner, spending, and order history, with approve/reject actions available for pending applications. When viewing a retailer's full profile, I can see their store info, owner contact details, address, GST, business hours, bank details, and registration date, plus buttons to approve or reject them. There's also a delivery settings area starting with warehouse location coordinates.

Now I'm thinking through the navigation structure—the customer app needs a bottom tab bar with Home, Search, Orders, and Profile across all main screens, while the admin side doesn't show a bottom nav in the PDF, so I'll use back arrows and a dashboard as the entry point. Actually, I should add a simple admin bottom nav with Dashboard, Orders, Catalog, and Retailers for consistency. I'm about to start writing all the code files, beginning with the core infrastructure and then moving through each screen component.

For the phone frame wrapper, I'll handle it in App.tsx—making it 390px wide with a max height of 844px, centered on desktop with rounded corners and shadow, but full screen on mobile. I'm also considering how to use Tailwind v4's `@theme` directive to define design tokens like primary colors that can be used throughout as utilities.

Writing all the files now... Writing CSS styles... Adding animation utility classes... I'm checking the exact Tailwind v4 syntax for the `@theme` directive and how it maps color names to utilities. I could also just use inline styles or Tailwind's built-in violet scale, which should be close enough to the purple I need.

Actually, Tailwind's violet colors map perfectly to what I'm looking for—`violet-600` is exactly `#7c3aed`. So I'll skip the custom theme and just use Tailwind's violet palette throughout: `bg-violet-600` for primary, `text-violet-600` for text, lighter shades like `bg-violet-100` for backgrounds, and `bg-violet-700` for hover states. This is much simpler than trying to define custom theme values.

Writing component code... I'm mapping out the remaining screens and admin pages, so that's about 34 total files to create. Rather than write each one individually, I should batch some of the smaller components together for efficiency. I'm settling on grouping the screens into logical files to keep things manageable—auth flows together, product browsing together, commerce operations together, orders and account management separate, and admin screens in their own file. That gives me around a dozen files total which is much more practical than spreading everything out. Now I'm ready to start writing the actual code instead of continuing to plan the structure.

Writing TypeScript types... Defining the data structures... Defining the product categories... Defining the products array with detailed pricing tiers and stock information for each item... Adding more product entries... Defining more product entries... Defining product data for moong dal and turmeric powder with their respective stock levels, pricing, and descriptions. Adding more product entries... Adding more orders... Continuing with another order from Modern Traders with basmati rice and groundnut oil, totaling 3925 rupees and marked as delivered on cash on delivery...

now moving to a cancelled order from Verma Wholesale for chana dal that was placed on UPI but remains unpaid, followed by setting up the retailers data structure.

I'm defining the Sharma General Store retailer profile with contact details, banking information for HDFC Bank, and noting they were approved on March 15, 2025 with a total spend of 28.

450 across 12 orders. Now I'm adding another retailer, Modern Traders, owned by Anita Deshmukh with similar profile structure including her ICICI Bank account details. Adding more customer records... Continuing with more merchant records... Defining notification data and weekly order metrics...

Now I need to write out all the screen components. I'll start with the authentication screens, then move through home, products, commerce, account, and admin sections. For screen transitions, I'm planning to use a simple wrapper approach with a key-based animation class to handle the switching between views. I can batch write multiple independent screen files together since they don't depend on each other, so I'll organize them into groups and submit them efficiently. I'm thinking through the navigation animations—slide in from the right for forward navigation and from the left when going back feels more natural on mobile. I'll track the direction in context to apply the right animation. Now I'm ready to write out all the screen files with complete, production-ready code.

Writing component files... Writing CSS styles... Adding animation classes... Defining the Product interface with fields for name, category, pricing tiers, stock, and description, then setting up OrderItem and Order interfaces to track purchases with status tracking and payment information.

Now I'm laying out the Retailer interface to capture store details like owner info, banking credentials, and performance metrics, along with CartItem and AppNotification interfaces for managing shopping carts and user alerts.

I need to set up the app context to track the current screen, navigation parameters, history for back navigation, animation direction, cart contents, admin mode status, notifications, and the demo data state for managing retailer approvals and orders.

Writing context setup... Finishing the context type definition with retailer rejection and order management methods, then setting up the React context and provider component that initializes state for navigation, cart, and other app features. Writing component hooks... Adding notification and order management functions...

I'm wrapping everything in the context provider with all the state handlers and navigation functions exposed to the app, so components can access cart operations, admin controls, retailer approvals, and order management from anywhere.

Now I need to build out all the screen components. I'm organizing them into separate files by feature area—authentication screens, the home feed, product browsing, checkout flow, user account pages, and the full admin dashboard with its various management sections.

Before diving into the individual screens, I should set up a shared components file with reusable UI elements like the bottom navigation tabs, cart bar, back button, status badges, and toggle switches that multiple screens will need. Writing all screen files... Writing the complete implementations... Writing the component files... For the admin section, I'm adding an approval queue to the dashboard, then building out AdminOrders with filtering, AdminOrderDetail for status management and payment tracking, AdminCatalog with separate tabs for products and categories (each with their own add/edit flows), AdminRetailers showing approved and pending retailers with detail views for approvals, and AdminDeliverySettings for warehouse coordinates and delivery rates. I'm going to start implementing this with React hooks. Writing the SVG bar chart... Generating QR pattern... Generating matrix data... Generating matrix data... Writing the implementations...

Before I dive in, I need to fix a few things: the context shouldn't include `cartTotal` since that should be computed dynamically based on the cart contents, the `placeOrder` function needs to generate unique order IDs, and I'll handle the "Buy Again" section by showing a hardcoded list of frequently ordered products. Also, when a retailer gets rejected from the admin catalog, they'll be removed from the list.","signature":"","providerOptions":{}}
